slides.title: Real data is messy
slides.text: People make typos, answer twice or write numbers that cannot be true. Chart messy data and the chart tells the wrong story.
slides.alt: Twelve kids typed their pet: Cat, dog, Fish, Dog, d0g, Cat, Dog. Three of the dogs are spelled wrong.

slides.title: Clean it first
slides.text: Fix typos, merge true repeats and remove values that cannot be true. Never remove a row just because you do not like its answer.
slides.alt: Sports sign-ups with every kind of mess: soccer in lower case, Jo twice, Tenis misspelled, and an age of 120.

focus.cue: Jo again: already higher up the list, so merge it
A value that cannot be true: 120

slides.title: Pet survey clean-up
slides.text: Three misspellings of dog split one bar into four short bars. Clean first, then chart.
steps: grouped as typed: Dog 4, dog 1, d0g 1, Dgo 1
fix dog, d0g and Dgo to Dog
slides.alt: Grouped before cleaning: Dog 4, but dog, d0g and Dgo each get a short bar of their own.

focus.cue: Dog 4: only the dogs spelled right
dog, d0g, Dgo: three more dogs, split off

slides.title: Compare by percent
slides.text: Class A: 10 of 20 kids walk to school. Class B: 12 of 30. B has more walkers, but A is 50% and B is 40%. Percent is part divided by whole, times 100.
slides.alt: Walkers by class with percent on: Class A 10 of 20 is 50%, Class B 12 of 30 is 40%.

focus.cue: The % button turns counts into shares

a value far from the rest; check if it is real

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Data Detective at Clean-Up Crew and solve all 6 cases. Chart the data as it is first, then clean it and chart it again. What changed?
